title: Most probably trangle-free graphs
summary: The celebrated Mantel's theorem states that any triangle-free graph on $n$ vertices contains at most $\left\lfloor n^2/4\right\rfloor$ edges. It is natural to ask how many triangles must exist in a graph with more than $\left\lfloor n^2/4\right\rfloor$ edges--a problem known as the Erdős-Rademacher problem. In this paper, we propose a probabilistic variant of this classic problem.
